o: Druhého září zmizel herec Benda, mistr Jan Benda, jak se mu říkalo od té doby, co jediným rozběhem vystoupil na jednu z nejvyšších příčlí herecké slávy.
t: On the second of September the actor Benda disappeared — Master Jan Benda, as he had been called ever since the day he climbed, in a single bound, to one of the highest rungs of acting fame.

o: Totiž druhého září se nestalo docela nic; posluhovačka, která v devět hodin ráno přišla poklidit Bendův byt, našla zválenou postel a celý ten kančí nepořádek, který obyčejně Bendu obklopoval, jenom pan mistr nebyl doma; ale jelikož na tom nebylo nic neobvyklého, dala byt svým sumárním způsobem do pořádku a šla zase po svém.
t: The point is that on the second of September nothing much happened; the maid who came at nine in the morning to tidy Benda's flat found a rumpled bed and all that pigsty mess which usually surrounded Benda; only the master himself was not home; but since that was nothing unusual, she put the flat in order in her own summary fashion and went about her business again.

o: Dobrá. Ale od té doby nebylo po herci Bendovi ani památky.
t: Fine. But from that day on, there was no trace of the actor Benda.

o: Paní Marešová (totiž ta posluhovačka) se nepodivila příliš ani tomu; prosím vás, tihle herci, to vám je jako cikáni; kdopak ví, kam zas jel hrát nebo flámovat.
t: Mrs Marešová (that is, the maid) was not overly surprised by that either; for goodness' sake, these actors, they are like gypsies; who knows where he has gone off to perform or carouse.

o: Ale desátého září se strhla po herci Bendovi sháňka; měl přijít do divadla, kde se začínaly zkoušky na Krále Leara; když Benda nepřišel ani na třetí zkoušku, vzbudilo to přece jen nepokoj a z divadla telefonovali doktoru Goldbergovi, Bendovu příteli, neví-li, co se děje s Bendou.
t: But on the tenth of September a search was set on foot for the actor Benda; he was supposed to come to the theatre, where rehearsals for King Lear had begun; when Benda failed to show up even for the third rehearsal, it did raise some disquiet, and the theatre telephoned Doctor Goldberg, Benda's friend, to ask whether he knew what was going on with Benda.

o: Ten doktor Goldberg byl chirurg a vydělával ukrutné peníze na slepých střevech; to už je taková židovská specialita.
t: That Doctor Goldberg was a surgeon and made enormous money on blind appendices; that is a Jewish specialty, you know.

o: Jinak to byl tlustý člověk s tlustými zlatými brýlemi a tlustým zlatým srdcem; hořel pro umění, měl byt od podlahy po strop ověšený samými obrazy a oddaně miloval herce Bendu, který k němu choval přátelské opovržení a s jistou blahosklonností mu dovoloval, aby za něj platil; což, mezi námi, nebyla zrovna maličkost.
t: Otherwise he was a fat man with fat golden spectacles and a fat golden heart; he burned for art, his flat was hung from floor to ceiling with nothing but paintings, and he devotedly loved the actor Benda, who regarded him with friendly contempt and with a certain benevolence allowed him to pay for everything; which, between us, was hardly a small matter.

o: Tragická maska Bendova a zářící obličej doktora Goldberga (který pil jenom vodu), to už patřilo k sobě při všech těch sardanapalských flámech a divokých výtržnostech, které byly druhou stránkou proslulosti velkého mima.
t: Benda's tragic mask and the shining face of Doctor Goldberg (who drank only water) belonged together through all those Sardanapalian carousals and wild brawls, which were the other side of the great mime's renown.

o: Tedy tomu doktoru Goldbergovi telefonovali z divadla, co prý se děje s Bendou.
t: So it was to that Doctor Goldberg that the theatre telephoned, asking what was going on with Benda.

o: Odpověděl, že nemá ponětí, ale že se po něm podívá; co neřekl, bylo, že už ho sám po celý týden shání po všech nočních lokálech a výletních hotelech s rostoucím znepokojením; měl tísnivou předtuchu, že se něco Bendovi stalo.
t: He answered that he had no idea, but that he would look into it; what he did not say was that he had himself spent a whole week hunting for Benda in all the night spots and excursion hotels, with growing anxiety; he had a pressing foreboding that something had happened to Benda.

o: To bylo totiž tak: Doktor Goldberg byl, pokud mohl zjistit, poslední, kdo Jana Bendu viděl.
t: The fact was this: Doctor Goldberg was, as far as could be established, the last person to see Jan Benda.

o: Někdy koncem srpna s ním ještě podnikl triumfální tažení noční Prahou; ale pak už Benda nepřišel na žádnou obvyklou schůzku.
t: Once at the end of August he had still gone on a triumphal tour of nocturnal Prague with him; but after that Benda came to none of the usual meetings.

o: Snad stůně, řekl si konečně doktor Goldberg a zajel si jednou večer do Bendova bytu; bylo to právě prvního září.
t: Perhaps, thought Doctor Goldberg at last, and one evening drove over to Benda's flat; it was precisely the first of September.

o: Zvonil u dveří; nikdo nešel otevřít, ale uvnitř bylo slyšet nějaký šramot.
t: He rang at the door; nobody came to open it, but inside there was the sound of some clattering.

o: Tu drnčel doktor dobrých pět minut na zvonek; najednou zazněly kroky a dveře se otevřely; stál v nich Benda zahalený v županu, a doktor Goldberg se ho zděsil: tak zdivočele vypadal slavný herec s rozcuchanými a slepenými vlasy a vousy dobrý týden neholenými; zdál se přepadlý a špinavý. “A, to jste vy,” řekl nevlídně, “co chcete?”
t: There the doctor jingled the bell for a good five minutes; suddenly footsteps sounded and the door opened; Benda stood in it wrapped in a dressing gown, and Doctor Goldberg was horrified: the famous actor looked so wild, with tousled and matted hair and a beard unshaven for a good week; he seemed worn out and dirty. "Oh, it's you," he said ungraciously, "what do you want?"

o: “Proboha, copak se s vámi stalo?” vyhrkl doktor užasle.
t: "Good God, what has happened to you?" the doctor blurted out, dismayed.

o: “Nic,” zavrčel Benda. “Nikam nepůjdu, rozumíte?
t: "Nothing," growled Benda. "I'm not going anywhere, you understand?

o: Dejte mi pokoj!”
t: Leave me alone!"

o: A zavřel dveře Goldbergovi před nosem.
t: And he shut the door in Goldberg's face.

o: - Den nato tedy zmizel.
t: - So that day he simply vanished.

o: Doktor Goldberg brejlil ustaraně svými tlustými skly.
t: Doctor Goldberg fussed about, peering through his thick glasses.

o: Něco tu nebylo v pořádku.
t: Something was not right here.

o: Od domovníka baráku, kde Benda bydlel, zvěděl jenom to, že onehdy v noci, snad to bylo zrovna na druhého září, zastavilo asi ve tři hodiny ráno před domem auto; ale nikdo nevystoupil, jen troubil na houkačku, jako by dával někomu v domě znamení.
t: From the doorman of the tenement where Benda lived, he learned only that one night, perhaps it was right around the second of September, a car stopped in front of the house at about three in the morning; but nobody got out, it just honked its horn, as if signalling someone inside the house.

o: Pak bylo slyšet, že někdo vychází z domu a zabouchl za sebou domovní vrata; potom auto odjelo.
t: Then there was the sound of someone coming out of the house and slamming the street door behind them; after that the car drove off.

o: Jaké to bylo auto, kdepak, na to se domovník nešel podívat; ve tři hodiny ráno člověk neleze z postele, když nemusí.
t: What kind of car it was, where it came from, the doorman did not care to find out; at three in the morning a man does not get out of bed when he doesn't have to.

o: Ale ta houkačka troubila, jako by ti lidé měli hrozný kvalt a nemohli chvilku čekat.
t: But that horn did sound, as if those people were in a terrible hurry and couldn't wait a moment.

o: Paní Marešová vypověděla, že pan mistr celej tejden nevyšel z bytu (leda snad v noci), neholil se a snad se ani nemyl, jak vypadal; jídlo si nechal nosit domů, chlastal koňak a válel se na sofa; to jako je všecko.
t: Mrs. Marešová testified that the master had not set foot outside his apartment all that week (unless perhaps at night), he did not shave, and perhaps did not even wash, judging by how he looked; he had his food brought home, drank brandy and sprawled on the sofa; and that, she said, was all.

o: Nyní, když se začali o Bendovo zmizení starat také jiní lidé, šel doktor Goldberg znovu za paní Marešovou.
t: Now that other people had also begun to take an interest in Benda's disappearance, Doctor Goldberg went to see Mrs. Marešová again.

o: “Poslouchejte, matko,” řekl, “nevíte, jaké měl pan Benda na sobě šaty, když odešel ze svého bytu?”
t: "Listen, mother," he said, "do you know what clothes Mr. Benda had on when he left his apartment?"

o: “Žádný,” pravila paní Marešová; “to je právě to, co se mně nelíbí.
t: "None," said Mrs. Marešová; "that's exactly what I don't like about it.

o: Neměl žádný šaty.
t: He had no clothes on.

o: Já znám všecky jeho vobleky a všecky visej v bytě, - ani jedny katě nechyběj.”
t: I know all his suits, and they're all hanging in the apartment - not a single one is missing."

o: “Že by byl odešel jenom v prádle?” mínil doktor Goldberg velmi zaražen.
t: "Could it be that he left in his underwear?" Doctor Goldberg ventured, very worried.

o: “Ani v prádle ne,” prohlásila paní Marešová, “ani v botách; to je to divný, pane.
t: "Not even in his underwear," declared Mrs. Marešová, "nor in his shoes; it's a strange thing, sir.

o: Viděj, já mám zapsanej každej jeho kousek prádla, protože to nosím do prádelny; teď to vyprali a já jsem mu to srovnala a spočítala; má tam vosmnáct košil, nechybí ani jedna, ani jeden kapesník, no dočista nic.
t: You see, I have every piece of his clothing written down, because I take it to the laundry; they've just washed it and I sorted and counted it for him; he has eighteen shirts there, not one missing, not one handkerchief, absolutely nothing.

o: Jenom jeden kufírek je pryč, co s sebou vždycky bere.
t: Only one suitcase is gone, the one he always took with him.

o: Jestli vodešel, tak musel bejt krom ty drahý duše docela nahej.”
t: If he went away, he must have been quite close to you, dear soul.

o: Doktor Goldberg vypadal velmi povážlivě. “Matko,” řekl, “když jste tam druhého září ráno přišla, nebyl tam nějaký zvláštní nepořádek?
t: Doctor Goldberg looked very grave. "Madam," he said, "when you came there on the morning of September the second, was there any unusual disorder?

o: Víte, něco pokáceného nebo vylomené dveře - ?”
t: You know, something broken, or a door forced open -?"

o: “Nepořádek,” mínila paní Marešová, “to von tam nepořádek byl, jako vždycky.
t: "Disorder," said Mrs. Marešová, "there was no disorder there, as always.

o: Von pan Benda byl takový čuně, pane.
t: Mr. Benda was such a rascal, sir.

o: Ale jináč tam nebyl žádnej nepořádek, to zas ne.
t: But otherwise there was no disorder, that I don't know.

o: Ale řeknou mně, kam moh jít, když neměl na těle ani tu kšandu?”
t: But tell me, where could he go when he didn't even have a shirt on him?"

o: Doktor Goldberg to ovšem věděl tak málo jako ona; a s nejpochmurnějšími starostmi se obrátil tentokrát už na policii.
t: Doctor Goldberg knew that as little as she did; and with the most gloomy thoughts he turned this time to the police.

o: “Nu dobře,” řekl policejní úředník, když mu dr. Goldberg vyklopil všechno, co věděl, “budeme pátrat.
t: "All right," said the police officer, when Dr. Goldberg had told him everything he knew, "we will investigate.

o: Ale podle toho, co jste povídal, že byl po celý týden zamčen doma, neholený a nemytý, válel se na pohovce, chlastal koňak a pak se ztratil nahý jako ašant, to by, pane, koukalo, hm, na nějaké -“
t: But according to what you said, that he was shut in at home all week, unshaven and unwashed, sprawled on the sofa, swilling brandy and then vanished naked as an ass, that would look, sir, hm, like some -"

o: “- delirium,” vyhrkl doktor Goldberg.
t: "- delirium," blurted out Dr. Goldberg.

o: “Ano,” řekl úředník. “Řekněme na sebevraždu v pomatení smyslů.
t: "Yes," said the officer. "Let's say suicide in an insane state of mind.

o: Víte, u něho bych se tomu nedivil.”
t: I wouldn't be surprised with him."

o: “Ale to by se snad našlo jeho tělo,” mínil dr. Goldberg nejistě. “A potom, jakpak daleko by mohl dojít nahý?
t: "But his body would presumably be found," said Dr. Goldberg uncertainly. "And then, how far could he get, naked?

o: A proč by bral s sebou kufřík?
t: And why would he take the suitcase with him?

o: A ten vůz, co čekal u domu - Pane, to vypadá spíš jako útěk.”
t: And that cart waiting at the house - sir, that looks more like a flight."

o: “A co,” vzpomněl si úředník, “dluhy neměl?”
t: "And what," the officer recalled, "did he have debts?"

o: “Ne,” řekl honem doktor; on sice Jan Benda měl dluhů jako kvítí, ale nebral je nikdy tragicky.
t: "No," said the doctor quickly; he knew well enough that Jan Benda had debts like flowers, but he never took them tragically.

o: “Nebo… řekněme nějaký osobní skandál… nešťastnou lásku, nebo lues, nebo vůbec nějakou větší starost?”
t: "Or... let's say some personal scandal... an unhappy love affair, or syphilis, or some greater trouble of any kind?"

o: “Pokud vím, nic,” mínil doktor Goldberg váhavě; na jednu nebo dvě věci si přitom vzpomněl, ale spolkl je, - ostatně to všecko stěží mělo co dělat s nepochopitelným zmizením herce Bendy.
t: "As far as I know, nothing," the doctor Goldberg said reluctantly; he did recall one or two things, but swallowed them back—after all, none of that had much to do with the inexplicable disappearance of the actor Benda.

o: Nicméně když se vracel z policie domů - to se rozumí, policie učiní, co je v její moci -, převaloval v hlavě, co věděl o Bendovi po téhle stránce.
t: Nevertheless, as he was returning from the police station to his home—that is to say, the police would do everything in their power—he turned over in his mind what he knew about Benda in that respect.

o: Nebylo toho mnoho:.
t: It wasn't much:

o: 1. Benda měl někde za hranicemi legitimní manželku, o kterou se ovšem nestaral;.
t: 1. Benda had somewhere beyond the border a legitimate wife, whom, however, he did not look after;

o: 2. vydržoval si jakési děvče v Holešovicích;.
t: 2. he kept some girl in Holešovice;

o: 3. měl poměr, a sice takzvaný pohoršující poměr s paní Grétou, ženou velikého fabrikanta Korbela; ta paní Gréta chtěla mermomocí hrát divadlo, a proto pan Korbel financoval nějaké filmy, ve kterých jeho paní hrála ovšem hlavní role.
t: 3. he had an affair—a so-called scandalous affair—with Mrs. Gréta, the wife of the great manufacturer Korbel; this Mrs. Gréta was bent on acting the theater at all costs, and so Mr. Korbel financed certain films in which his wife played, of course, the leading parts.

o: Bylo tedy známo, že Benda je milencem paní Gréty, že paní Gréta za ním jezdí a už si ani nedává tak pozor, jak by se slušelo.
t: So it was known that Benda was Mrs. Gréta's lover, that Mrs. Gréta went after him and no longer even took care how she ought to.

o: Ostatně Benda nikdy o těchhle věcech nemluvil; pohrdal vším zpola s veličenskou důstojností a zpola s cynismem, který Goldberga mrazil.
t: Benda, moreover, never spoke of such things; he scorned everything half with haughty dignity and half with a cynicism that made Goldberg shudder.

o: Ne, řekl si doktor beznadějně, v soukromých věcech Bendových se nikdo nevyzná.
t: No, the doctor told himself hopelessly, nobody can make sense of Benda's private affairs.

o: Ať se propadnu, není-li v tom nějaká ošklivá historie; ale teď už je to věc policie.
t: Well, if there isn't some ugly story in it; but now it's a matter for the police.

o: Doktor Goldberg ovšem nevěděl, co policie podniká a jaké jsou její cesty: čekal s rostoucí malomyslností, že dostane nějakou zprávu.
t: Doctor Goldberg, however, did not know what the police were up to or what their ways were: he waited with growing despondency for some message.

o: Zatím už uplynul měsíc od zmizení herce Bendy a o Janu Bendovi se začalo mluvit v minulém čase.
t: Meanwhile, a month had already passed since the disappearance of the actor Benda, and Jan Benda had begun to be spoken of in the past tense.

o: Jednou kvečeru potkal doktor Goldberg starého herce Lebdušku; a jak se tak zapovídali, přišla řeč, to se rozumí, na Bendu. “Panečku, to byl herec,” vzpomínal starý Lebduška. “Já ho pamatuju, když mu bylo asi pětadvacet let.
t: One evening Doctor Goldberg ran into the old actor Lebduška; and as they fell to chatting, the talk came, of course, to Benda. "Young man, he was an actor," the old Lebduška recalled. "I remember him when he was about twenty-five years old.

o: Zatracený kluk, ten hrál Osvalda!
t: Damned fellow, he played Oswald!

o: Víte, že se tam chodili dívat mladí medikové, jak vypadá paralýza?
t: You know, the young medical students used to go there to see what paralysis looks like.

o: Tehdy hrál poprvé krále Leara; poslouchejte, já ani nevím, jak hrál, protože jsem se mu pořád díval na ruce.
t: That was when he first played King Lear; listen, I don't even know how he acted, because I kept watching his hands.

o: On vám měl ruce jako osmdesátiletý dědek, takové vyzáblé, vysušené, ubohé ruce - teda tomu podnes nerozumím, jak si udělal ty ruce.
t: He had hands like an eighty-year-old grandfather, such bony, withered, pitiful hands—well, I don't understand to this day how he managed to make those hands.

o: Já přece se taky dovedu maskovat; ale tohle, pane, po Bendovi neudělá nikdo; to ocení jenom herec.”
t: I can disguise myself all the same; but this, sir, nobody after Benda could do; only an actor can appreciate that."

o: Doktoru Goldbergovi působilo melancholickou rozkoš naslouchat tomu hereckému nekrologu na Jana Bendu.
t: It was a melancholic pleasure for Doctor Goldberg to listen to that actor's obituary for Jan Benda.

o: “To byl důkladný hráč, pane,” vzdychl Lebduška. “Jak vám sekýroval divadelního krejčího!
t: "He was a thorough artist, sir," Lebduška sighed. "How he sewed up the theater tailor!"

o: Já vám nebudu hrát krále, křičel, když mně dáte na kabát takové šófl krajky!
t: I'm not going to play the king for you, screaming, when you put such gaudy lace on my coat!

o: To on nesnesl na sobě žádný divadelní švindl.
t: He couldn't bear any theatrical fake on him.

o: Když měl hrát Othella, tak vám proběhal všechny starožitnické krámy, až našel takový starý renezanční prsten; a ten musel mít na prstě, když hrál Othella.
t: When he was to play Othello, he went through all the antique shops until he found an old Renaissance ring; and he had to have it on his finger when he played Othello.

o: On říkal, že se mu líp hraje, když má na sobě něco pravého.
t: He said he played better when he was wearing something genuine.

o: To ani nebyla hra, to bylo zrovna… převtělení,” řekl Lebduška nejistě, nevěda, užil-li pravého slova. “A když hrál, byl vždycky v pauzách sprostý jako polír a zamykal se ve své šatně, aby ho nikdo nevytrhoval z toho stavu.
t: It wasn't even acting, it was more like… a transformation," Lebduška said uncertainly, not knowing whether he'd used the right word. "And when he played, in the intervals he was always as coarse as a polishing wheel, and he locked himself in his dressing room so that no one could drag him out of that state.

o: Proto on tolik pil, že mu to šlo na nervy,” mínil Lebduška zamyšleně. “Já jdu tadyhle do kina, pane,” řekl na rozloučenou.
t: That's why he drank so much, that it wore him down and got on his nerves," Lebduška said thoughtfully. "I'm going along to the cinema here, sir," he said in farewell.

o: “Já půjdu s vámi,” navrhl doktor Goldberg, nevěda, jak by utloukl večer.
t: "I'll come with you," Doctor Goldberg suggested, not knowing how else to spend the evening.

o: Dávali tam nějaký námořnický film, ale doktor Goldberg ani dobře nevěděl, oč jde; skoro se slzami v očích poslouchal, jak starý Lebduška žvatlá o Janu Bendovi.
t: They were showing some kind of naval film, but Doctor Goldberg didn't even really know what it was about; he listened almost with tears in his eyes as old Lebduška babbled about Jan Benda.

o: “To nebyl herec,” povídal Lebduška, “to byl zrovna čert; jemu nestačil jeden život, to je to.
t: "He wasn't an actor," Lebduška said, "he was the devil himself; one life wasn't enough for him, that's what it was.

o: V životě byl prase, pane doktore; ale na jevišti, to byl skutečný král nebo skutečný šupák.
t: In life he was a pig, Doctor; but on the stage, he was a real king or a real rascal.

o: Pane, jak on dovedl kynout rukou, jako by po celý život jenom poroučel; a zatím jeho táta byl potulný brusič.
t: Sir, how deftly he handles the brush, as if he had done nothing else all his life; and meanwhile his dad was a wandering knife-grinder.

o: Helejte, tady ten trosečník; je na pustém ostrově a přitom má ostříhané nehty, blbec jeden.
t: Look at this shaggy fellow; he's on a desert island and he has trimmed nails, the idiot.

o: Vidíte, jak ty fousy má jenom přilepené?
t: Do you see how his whiskers are just pasted on?

o: Kdyby ho hrál Benda, tak by si nechal narůst pravé fousy, a za nehty by měl pravou špínu…
t: If Benda played him, he'd have let real whiskers grow, and he'd have real dirt under his nails...

o: Copak, pane doktore, copak se vám tak najednou stalo?”
t: Come now, Doctor, come now, what has come over you all of a sudden?

o: “Promiňte,” koktal Goldberg, vstávaje, “ale já jsem si na něco vzpomněl.
t: "Excuse me," stammered Goldberg, rising, "but I've just remembered something.

o: Děkuju vám,” a už běžel z biografu.
t: "Thank you," and he was already running out of the biograph.

o: Benda by si byl nechal narůst pravé vousy, opakoval.
t: Benda would have let real whiskers grow, he repeated.

o: Benda si nechal narůst pravé vousy!
t: Benda would have let real whiskers grow!

o: Že mě to nenapadlo dřív!
t: Why didn't it occur to me before!

o: “Na četnické velitelství!” křikl, vrhaje se do nejbližšího taxíku; a když pronikl k strážmistrovi, který měl noční službu, domáhal se s velikým křikem a prošením, aby mu pro živého boha hned, ale hned zjistili, nebyla-li druhého září nebo někdy potom nalezena kdekoliv mrtvola neznámého vandráka, ano, kdekoliv prosím!
t: "To the police headquarters!" he shouted, throwing himself into the nearest taxi; and when he had pushed his way to the sergeant on night duty, he demanded with great shouting and pleading that they would, for God's sake, find out at once—at once—whether on the second of September or at some later time a corpse of an unknown tramp had been found anywhere, anywhere, please!

o: Proti všemu očekávání se onen strážmistr šel opravdu někam podívat nebo zeptat, spíše z dlouhé chvíle nežli ze zvláštní horlivosti nebo zájmu; zatím se doktor Goldberg potil rozčilením, neboť mu svítalo něco hrozného.
t: Against all expectation, the sergeant really did go somewhere to look or to ask, more out of boredom than out of any special eagerness or interest; meanwhile Doctor Goldberg was sweating with agitation, for something terrible was dawning on him.

t: "Well, sir," said the sergeant, returning, "on the second of September, in the morning, a gamekeeper found the corpse of an unknown tramp in the Křivoklát forests, about forty years old; on the third of September a corpse of an unknown man, about thirty years old, was pulled out of the Elbe near Litoměřice, he had been in the water at least fourteen days; on the tenth of September, near Německý Brod, an unknown hanged man, about sixty years old..."

o: “O tom tulákovi není nic bližšího?” ptal se doktor Goldberg bez dechu.
t: "Is there nothing more about that tramp?" asked Doctor Goldberg breathlessly.

t: "Murder," said the sergeant, looking intently at the agitated doctor. "According to the report from the police station, he had his skull smashed in with a blunt object.

t: In the photograph the body of a man was visible from the waist up; he was dressed in ragged clothes, with a torn calico shirt; where people have a forehead and eyes, there was only a horrible clump of matted hair and something that might have been skin or bone; so many bristles, a beard overgrown like a brush, and half-open mouth still resembled a human being.

o: Té noci doktor Goldberg podnikl zase tah noční Prahou; pil svou sklenici vody ve všech lokálech, kde kdysi kraloval Jan Benda, a brejlil svými zlatými okuláry po všech koutech, ale Benda nebyl nikde.
t: That night Doctor Goldberg undertook another round of nocturnal Prague; he drank his glass of water in all the pubs where Jan Benda had once reigned, and peered with his golden spectacles into every corner, but Benda was nowhere.

o: K ránu doktor Goldberg zbledl, řekl si nahlas, že je idiot, a hnal se do své garáže.
t: By morning Doctor Goldberg had gone pale, said aloud that he was an idiot, and rushed off to his garage.

o: Ráno už byl u jednoho okresního hejtmanství a nechal si vzbudit hejtmana; naštěstí se ukázalo, že toho pána už jednou vlastnoručně vykuchal a zašil a odevzdal mu na památku slepé střevo naložené v lihu.
t: In the morning he was already at one district governor's office and had himself roused the governor; luckily it turned out that he had once personally butchered that gentleman and, as a keepsake, presented him with a blind gut packed in alcohol.

t: As a result of this more than superficial acquaintance, within two hours he had an exhumation permit in hand and stood at the side of a very indignant district doctor while the body of an unknown tramp was dug up.

t: "I don't know," the doctor said with distaste. "Colleague, by now you can't tell anything about him; I beg you, if it's been a month in the ground—".

t: When the grave had been dug out, Doctor Goldberg had to send for spirits; otherwise he couldn't have got the gravediggers to lift and carry to the mortuary the unspeakable thing that lay at the bottom of the grave, sewn up in a sack.

o: Za chvíli se motal z márnice doktor Goldberg, na smrt bledý. “Pojďte se podívat,” řekl chraptivě, šel zpátky k tomu tělu a ukazoval na místo, které bylo kdysi hlava člověka.
t: A moment later Doctor Goldberg staggered out of the mortuary, deathly pale. "Come and look," he said hoarsely, went back to the body and pointed at the spot where a man's head had once been.

o: Tu odhrnul doktor Goldberg pinzetou to, co byly kdysi rty; objevily se odporně zkažené zuby, nebo spíše jen žluté kousky zubů, blýskající z černé karies. “Tak se dobře podívejte,” vydechl Goldberg, zajel pinzetou mezi zuby a vyňal z nich kus černého kazu.
t: There Doctor Goldberg pushed aside with forceps what had once been lips; horribly decayed teeth appeared, or rather only yellow fragments of teeth gleaming out of black caries. "Well, look at that closely," Goldberg breathed, slipped the forceps between the teeth and extracted a piece of black tartar.

o: Pod ním se ukázaly dva skvoucí, silné řezáky.

t: But Doctor Goldberg could bear it no longer; he fled from the mortuary, holding his head in both hands.

t: When he returned a moment later to the district doctor, he was pale and terribly sad. "So those remarkably decayed teeth of yours, colleague," he said quietly. "That was only black pitch, the stuff actors stick on their teeth when they play grandfathers or tramps.

t: That filthy bum was an actor, colleague," and he waved his hand hopelessly, adding: "And a great actor at that."

t: That day Doctor Goldberg turned up at the factory owner Korbel's; he was a big, strong man with a beard like a rubber boot and a body like a pillar.

t: "Sir," said Doctor Goldberg, peering intently through his round spectacles, "I come to you… about the actor Benda."

t: "But," said the manufacturer, folding his hands behind his head. "Has he turned up again?"

t: "In part," said Doctor Goldberg. "I think it will interest you… if only because of that film you wanted to make with him… that is, to finance."

t: "What film?" asked the big man indifferently. "I know nothing about it."

t: Sir, you'd expect him to dress himself down to the last stitch at the cuffs and the string around his waist like a proper scoundrel; that was always his thing, to make such a fuss about costume."

t: As it was arranged with Benda, you didn't go up, but you honked down below.

t: The man in the shadow began to laugh quietly. “Listen, my good man,” he said with a certain cheerfulness, “if you only knew for certain a tenth of what you have been calling me here, you wouldn't come to me with it, but to the police, would you?”
